text: Understanding Git branching is essential for modern software development. A branch lets you work on new features without affecting the main code. Developers create feature branches to add new functionality or fix bugs safely. Once the work is complete, merging combines those changes back into the main branch. Many teams use pull requests to review code before merging, which improves quality and encourages collaboration. This version control workflow keeps projects organised and reduces the risk of errors. By using branches, developers can experiment freely, work in parallel, and maintain a stable codebase. Learning these basic Git concepts will make you a more confident and effective team member.
